arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Smith argued the parties agree on the core legal issue. He stated the question concerns prevailing defendants in Title VII cases.
Mr. Fletcher disputed the characterization of the 2013 dismissal. He emphasized the original 2009 dismissal as the relevant event.
Justice Sotomayor noted that judges must decide the final outcome. She questioned whether merits labels alone suffice for fee decisions.

paragraphs: The case tests the standard for awarding attorney fees in Title VII suits. The lower court denied fees. The parties dispute whether a merits ruling is required.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: CRST Van Expedited wants the fee award restored. It argues the dismissal ended the case in its favor.
The EEOC wants the fee denial upheld. It argues no merits ruling occurred to justify fees.

paragraphs: CRST Van Expedited argues a dismissal with prejudice suffices for fees. It contends the case ended in the defendant's favor.
The EEOC argues fees require a merits determination. It asserts the dismissal did not resolve the underlying claims.

paragraphs: This dispute defines the scope of fee awards in employment discrimination cases. It clarifies when a dismissal qualifies as a prevailing outcome. The standard affects litigation costs for employers and agencies nationwide.
